content:
tara.g: Heads up — we're still seeing ~10-20% of requests where metrics (cost counters) and traces can't be correlated for per-request cost attribution. Root cause looks like inconsistent correlation keys across SDKs and edge proxies. Anyone on a concrete plan?

ben_k: Oof. Is this mostly missing trace_id, or is it different IDs (trace_id vs request_id vs x-correlation)?

tara.g: Mixed bag. Some services send trace_id in header, some send an internal request_id, and edge proxies sometimes rewrite headers. Also sampling drops traces but metrics still emit.

samuel: For short-term: we can fallback to a best-effort join using timestamp+service+path for low-cardinality cases. Works for dashboards but sucks for exact billing.

irene: That fallback will produce false-positives at high QPS. Cardinality explosion if we add request_id as a tag in metrics. Concerned about storage/cost.

matt_ops: Agree with irene. Two tradeoffs: 1) Add a canonical correlation header that every client/edge sets (low-effort but requires rollout). 2) Build a lightweight correlation service that maps multiple IDs -> canonical id at ingress. Option 2 centralizes logic but is extra infra.

julie_prod: From product side, accuracy matters for reserved capacity chargebacks. We need deterministic mapping for 99.9% of traffic. Is there a hybrid?

ben_k: Hybrid = canonical header + late-binding lookup. Emit metrics with best-effort header if present; at ingest time try to resolve via lookup table for edge cases. The lookup table could be TTL cache of recent mappings.

irene: TTL cache sounds reasonable. But need to bound memory; we should avoid full tenant-wide mapping in RAM. Propose sharded LRU with per-tenant budget and eviction policy that logs misses to sampling pipeline.

tara.g: Example headers we see now: 
```
Traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
X-Request-Id: a1b2c3d4
X-Redwood-Correlation: rw-xyz-000
```
Goal: pick one canonical header name and policy.

matt_ops: I propose `X-Redwood-Correlation` as canonical. Implementation notes: SDKs set it if trace present, proxies propagate and avoid rewrite, and ingress correlation service resolves when only request_id present.

julie_prod: Timeline? Customers want fix before next billing cycle in ~3 weeks.

ben_k: Rollout plan: phase 0 = opt-in flag + edge-proxy passthrough + SDK change (2 weeks). Phase 1 = correlation service + ingest enrichment (3rd week). Phase 2 = retro-run reconciliation for last 7 days of metrics (post-deploy).

irene: Need schema change in telemetry: metrics should include optional `correlation_id` tag (low-cardinality index) + provenance tag (`correlation_resolution: header|ingest_lookup|fallback`). That helps later audits.

samuel: Also account for sampling: if trace was sampled out, we still want metrics to keep correlation_id when available; otherwise mark `sampled=false`.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline: correlation-service v0.1 pushed to canary cluster at 1759995600, ingress-enrichment flag enabled.

tara.g: Actionables: 1) @ben_k draft SDK header change PR (due EOD Fri). 2) @matt_ops stand up correlation-service canary + doc (due Wed). 3) @irene update metrics producer schema & retention/cost estimate (due Tue). 4) @julie_prod prepare customer comms and billing impact note (due next Thu).

ben_k: I’ll start the SDK PR now. If anyone has objections to header name (X-Redwood-Correlation) call them out here.

irene: No objection. +1 to adding provenance tag.

matt_ops: I'll post the lightweight design doc to eng-platform later today. It will include TTL sizing and cost calc.

julie_prod: I’ll draft customer-facing note with rollback plan.

tara.g: Thanks all. We'll sync next week in the observability sync. :thumbsup:
